# 5.1 Experimental Setup We use Qwen3-8B as the base model and perform supervised fine-tuning on high-quality SFT data, followed by further optimization with constructed DPO preference pairs. Detailed training procedures and hyperparameter settings can be found in Appendix A.5. During evaluation, we use the Serper $\mathsf{API}^1$ for web search and Jina $^2$ for webpage content extraction. Retrieved webpages are summarized using DeepSeek-V3.1. We evaluate our method on six challenging benchmarks: GAIA [15], BrowseComp-zh/en [27, 33], HLE [17], XBench-DeepSearch [1], and WebWalkerQA [29]. As in prior deep research studies, we use the text subsets for GAIA and HLE. We compare our approach with foundation models and deep research agents. Model performance is reported using the pass@1 metric. # 5.2 Main Results Table 3 summarizes the main evaluation results of 0f fSeeker across six challenging deep-research benchmarks. Online RL is Not All You Need. OffSeeker attains top-tier performance among agents of comparable scale and matches models with up to 30B parameters that are trained using online RL. Across all benchmarks, it delivers consistently strong results, indicating that advanced deep-research capabilities can be realized solely through offline training, and that online RL is not all you need for effective deep-research modeling. On BrowseComp-zh, OffSeeker achieves a score of 26.6, surpassing medium-scale systems such as WebSailor-32B (25.5) and Table 3 Main results on deep research benchmarks. All scores of 0ffSeeker are computed as Pass@1 using LLM-as-Judge. BC-zh and BC-en denote the BrowseComp-ZH and BrowseComp benchmarks, respectively, while XBench-DS refers to XBench-DeepSearch. Scores marked with $\dagger$ are reported from our own tests, others are reported from official reports or other deep research works. For GAIA and HLE, we use text-only subset of the original benchmarks. Importantly, these results are obtained without any online RL, whereas many competitors depend on extensive and costly online fine-tuning. Among agents below 10B parameters, OffSeeker consistently ranks at the top, significantly outperforming open-source baselines such as ASearcher and DeepDive on BrowseComp-zh, BrowseComp-en, and XBench-DS. All improvements over baseline models are statistically significant $(p < 0.05)$ . OffSeeker Can Generalize Effectively. Although the training data primarily targets deep search tasks, OffSeeker exhibits strong generalization across diverse task categories. For example, on the HLE benchmark, OffSeeker (DPO) attains a score of 13.8, matching or surpassing models trained with online reinforcement learning, including WebExplorer-8B and ASearcher-Web-QwQ. This result is particularly significant because HLE involves reasoning patterns distinct from standard search tasks. We attribute this success to the model's ability to internalize high-level complicated problem-solving strategies, rather than merely memorizing search patterns. The consistent performance beyond the training domain underscores the effectiveness of our offline preference-based approach, showing that high-quality preference data can yield robust and transferable reasoning capabilities. ![](images/2601.18467/27c18b45d4fb0069ce21e8b1ba7a0ca5a21475d9a835d639e47e5845a32faf55.jpg) Figure 4 Pass@1 accuracy $(\%)$ on BrowseComp-zh for different SFT models and dataset sizes. For our model, all tasks are generated by DeepForge. ![](images/2601.18467/1a39f4c8b93ff1f91f856e8cba0502895e305af62364ffa792172e6dab75e0a2.jpg) Figure 5 OffSeeker test accuracy $(\%)$ on GAIA and BrowseComp-ZH with different context window sizes. Offline RL Training Achieves Competitive Results. The comparison between the SFT and DPO variants highlights the benefits of our offline DPO methodology. DPO consistently enhances performance across all benchmarks: +3.9 on GAIA, +2.4 on BrowseComp-zh, +2.2 on BrowseComp-en, +2.1 on HLE, +1.0 on XBench-DeepSearch, and +1.7 on WebWalkerQA. These consistent gains confirm that advanced deep-research competency can be attained through offline preference optimization. Moreover, our offline framework incurs no API costs during training, offers greater stability, and provides a cost-efficient paradigm for academic researchers, advancing our goal of enabling accessible development of deep-research agents.
